story.title: Federal Appeals Court Blocks Trump's Third-Country Deportation Policy
story.summary: A federal appeals court has ruled against the Trump administration's policy of deporting individuals to third countries where they have no ties. The court stated that U.S. immigration officials must provide detainees with a meaningful opportunity to contest such deportations. This decision affects over 25,000 deportations that had already occurred under the policy.

timeline_highlights.summary: US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) is preparing to target over 300,000 Haitians who will lose their legal protections under the Temporary Protected Status (TPS) program. Plans reportedly include arresting migrants in various states, such as Ohio, and expediting their deportation to Haiti, which is currently facing significant crises.

event_overview.title: About Immigration Policy
event_overview.subject: Immigration Policy
event_overview.summary: This event concerns U.S. immigration-enforcement and removal policy, particularly the use of detention, immigration-court proceedings, deportation flights, and changes to humanitarian or procedural protections. The selected developments focus on how federal executive actions and court rulings can affect specific groups of noncitizens, including Haitian nationals and people seeking asylum.

facts.label: Legal framework
facts.value: U.S. removal proceedings are governed principally by the Immigration and Nationality Act; modern removal proceedings replaced the former separate deportation and exclusion processes on April 1, 1997.

facts.label: Agencies and courts
facts.value: DHS enforces immigration law through components including ICE, while the Justice Department's Executive Office for Immigration Review administers immigration courts and the Board of Immigration Appeals. Immigration judges decide removability and applications for relief, subject to administrative appeal.

facts.label: How a removal case begins
facts.value: In ordinary immigration-court removal cases, DHS serves and files a Notice to Appear (Form I-862); the notice states the nature and legal basis of the proceeding and the alleged conduct supporting removability.

facts.label: Execution of removal orders
facts.value: After a final removal order, federal law generally provides a 90-day removal period, during which the government is directed to remove the person, subject to statutory exceptions and case-specific legal constraints.

facts.label: Haiti and Temporary Protected Status
facts.value: Temporary Protected Status (TPS) is a statutory, temporary protection that bars removal and authorizes employment for eligible beneficiaries while it is in effect; DHS's 2025 termination notice set the Haiti TPS designation to end at 11:59 p.m. local time on February 3, 2026.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline tracks notable 2026 enforcement, protection-expiration, deportation, visa, and litigation developments; it does not attempt to catalog every immigration case, removal flight, agency action, or policy affecting all noncitizens.

related_stories.title: Panic and Protests Follow Deaths of 37 Miners in Nigerian Custody
related_stories.summary: In Nigeria, 37 suspected illegal gold miners died while in custody, prompting protests in Minna. Survivors described a harrowing struggle for breath in an overcrowded prison cell. In response to the unrest, police fired teargas at demonstrators and imposed a curfew. Authorities are investigating the cause of the deaths, with some reports indicating overcrowding and poor ventilation may have contributed.

related_stories.title: Casualties from Police HQ Attack in Pakistan Reach 31
related_stories.summary: The death toll from an attack on a police headquarters in Kohat, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province, Pakistan, has risen to at least 31. The incident involved both an explosion and a gun assault, with local officials confirming the updated figures following the attack on September 18.

related_stories.title: Smoke and Flames Erupt Near Riyadh Airport Amid Air Raid Alerts
related_stories.summary: Flames and a large plume of smoke were observed near Riyadh's main airport following overnight air raid alerts issued by Saudi authorities. The alerts were prompted by escalating attacks from Yemen's Houthi group, marking the first such warnings for the capital since the conflict intensified in July. Residents reported hearing loud explosions, and firefighters responded to a fire at a fuel tank near the airport.

related_stories.title: Juror in Clancy Trial Expresses Certainty of Guilt in Children's Deaths
related_stories.summary: A juror who opposed the acquittal of Lindsay Clancy has publicly stated he had no doubts about her guilt in the deaths of her three children. This marks the first time he has spoken out about his decision, claiming that other jurors did not heed his conviction. His comments were made through a statement released by his lawyer.
